title: A coupled drag orbit fits 22 ASASSN-14ko event times while its period changes within the X-ray clock segment
abstract: We test whether cumulative torque destroys a proposed precessing drag clock for ASASSN-14ko. A coupled two-crossing impulse map updates orbital energy, angular momentum, eccentricity, inclination, travel time and secular relativistic precession. In one fixed mass and steady disc case, it fits eight published X-ray suppression times and fourteen optical half-rise times with negative log likelihood 26.106 and X-ray chi-square 2.569. The semi-latus rectum grows 5.84 percent across cycles 5-39. The osculating period spans 107.953-108.908 days within cycles 20-33, while model event times at the X-ray cycle positions depart from their best line by at most 0.611 day. Thus a nearly straight sampled clock can remain compatible with a coupled changing orbit. The fit survives the torque feedback omitted by an earlier frozen clock. This is a conditional existence result, not a detection of drag. The model fixes the black-hole mass and disc, uses constant marker lags, and omits stellar mass loss, disc response and full relativistic trajectories. No new telescope data or calibrated mechanism test is claimed. Code, source hashes, synthetic trajectories, aggregate results and independent numerical checks are provided.

display.caption: Synthetic event clock and coupled orbit changes for the selected 25-degree example. Points show model values at the X-ray cycle positions, not measured times.
